question.text: The definition of 'foreign exchange derivative contract' under FEMA excludes contracts involving currencies of which two countries?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under FEMA, a "foreign exchange derivative contract" derives value from a change in the exchange rate of two currencies (at least one not INR) or from a change in a foreign currency interest rate. Contracts involving the currencies of Nepal and Bhutan are explicitly excluded from this definition. The Trap: The exclusion is specific to Nepal and Bhutan; other neighbouring or major-economy currencies (Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, China, Russia) are not part of the FEMA exclusion list referenced here. Note: Source: page 38 of the NISM Series-I workbook, which sets out the FEMA definition and the Nepal/Bhutan exclusion.
